prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane receding along a snow-covered trail flanked by bare trees at 5–15 m and a distant treeline beyond 20 m, while clearly separating foreground entities from the bright white snow. In frame 1, the person in the jacket stands roughly 1.8–2.2 m ahead and slightly right of center with a blue sled on the ground to the lower left at about 1.5–2 m and the front edge of a utility vehicle partially visible at the far right edge at ~1.5 m; across frames 2 and 3, the camera wearer turns left toward the open path so these objects move out of view, then turns back right in frames 4 and 5 as the person approaches from ~2.2 m to ~1.2–1.5 m in front of the parked utility vehicle (~2.5–3.5 m away to the right and behind the person). In frame 5, a bright white silhouette at the bottom right shows the camera wearer's gloved hand at ~0.3–0.5 m reaching within arm's reach of the tether held in the person's left hand (~1.0–1.2 m away), while the person partially occludes the front left side of the vehicle in frames 4 and 5. Compared to RGB, the depth map makes the 3D separation between the white-hatted person, the white snow, the thin vertical saplings, and the dark utility vehicle much easier to gauge, though it looks unreliable where the person's extended left hand and rope in frame 4 flare into an overly bright blob and where fine tree branches blur into the dark sky.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground objects in frames 1, 4, and 5 while leaving frames 2 and 3 completely empty as the camera pans left across the unoccupied snowy trail and trees. In frame 1, it segments the person at ~2 m in the center-right, the blue sled at the bottom left (~1.5–2 m away and ~0.5 m left of the person's feet), and a sliver of the vehicle at the far right edge (~1.5 m away); after the camera turns back right in frames 4 and 5, the person's mask grows larger and shifts lower as they step closer from ~2.2 m to ~1.2–1.5 m with their torso and blurred face oriented toward the camera wearer. While the person holds a coiled rope within their own arm's reach in frame 4 and brings the handle within arm's reach of the camera wearer's lower-right hand in frame 5, the segmentation map completely misses the camera wearer's gloved hand at the bottom right of frame 5 as well as the entire black utility vehicle sitting ~1 m behind and to the right of the person in frames 4 and 5. This map highlights the exact silhouette boundary of the person's legs and the ground contact region better than the low-contrast dark pants in RGB, but it is highly unreliable in class labeling—misclassifying the blue sled in frame 1 and the coiled rope near the person's feet in frame 4 as a 'snowboard', the vehicle edge in frame 1 as a 'person', and the pink jacket collar in frame 5 as a 'tie'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the person in front of the camera wearer in frames 1, 4, and 5, with no skeletons present in frames 2 and 3 when the camera wearer turns left away from the person. Across the active frames, the facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) are centered between the shoulders and oriented toward the camera wearer, while the shoulder-to-hip torso trapezoid widens and drops lower in the frame from frame 4 (~2.2 m away) to frame 5 (~1.2–1.5 m away) as the person steps closer and leans slightly forward. Both of the person's arms hang down within ~0.3–0.5 m of their hips and thighs, with their left wrist positioned lower and slightly inward in frames 4 and 5 where they hold the tether within arm's reach of the camera wearer's hand in frame 5. The skeleton makes the person's torso orientation, slight forward stoop in frame 5, and limb symmetry under bulky winter clothing much clearer than RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable where the lower body is truncated below the hips in frame 1 even though the person's legs are visible in RGB, where magenta hand keypoints are completely missing and replaced only by coarse yellow wrist clusters, and where the camera wearer's own visible right hand at the bottom of frame 5 is not detected at all.
